text:
Sequential counterfactual methods emphasize plausible, minimal edits: [CETD](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/13/20/11176) models temporal dependencies when generating replacement histories; [TRACE](https://github.com/devUuung/TRACE) combines position selection, plausibility-aware substitute retrieval and ranking-margin evaluation, including BERT4Rec. Neither establishes a universal control for every confound. [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) uses masked-item training; diagnostics should preserve appended-mask inference, padding and the prediction position.

Recommended design, synthesized from these principles: compare equal-sized recent and older windows using substitutions matched on training-frequency bins, repeat status/multiplicity and title/description similarity; constrain contextual plausibility using public training histories. Replace tokens in place, preserving length and positional indices. Add paired swaps of recent/older blocks to preserve the exact item multiset and popularity distribution while changing placement. Substitution measures sensitivity to identity/content at fixed positions; swaps measure sensitivity to arrangement. Neither alone isolates recency from learned absolute position: use a separate position-offset probe with unchanged item order and relative distances to the prediction mask, where supported, and report it as positional sensitivity. Compare paired changes in target score, rank and validation HR@10 across replacement draws, with uncertainty.

Prioritize matched substitutions plus the multiset-preserving swap control. If replacements remain out of distribution, conclusions concern the frozen model’s response to those specified corruptions—not causal user preferences or clean-history recency importance. Larger recent-window damage can reflect greater implausibility there. The [ROAR study](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2019/file/fe4b8556000d0f0cae99daa5c5c5a410-Paper.pdf) explicitly identifies this ambiguity; retraining changes the model being explained. Agreement across plausible substitutions and swaps strengthens evidence of positional dependence but does not eliminate confounding.
